snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), on \(E_P\), the sets \(K_C(P)\), indexed by \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), form a partition of \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\), every \(K_C(P)\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\), and \(I_C\) contains \(\nu_P(K_C(P))\). Moreover, with a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), singleton associated clusters have support-interval length at most \(C r_{n,\alpha}\), their mass intervals have length at most \(C\min\{1,r_{n,\alpha}/\delta(P)\}\), and every associated cluster has \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)\le C\min\{1,r_{n,\alpha}/\Delta_C(P)\}\). Finally, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge1-\alpha\). Thus effects unresolved at the \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\) scale are merged without making the true-cluster association or its external gap implicit.

snapshot.stmt:
The upper and lower bounds on the same uniformly conditioned causal VMW submodel imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\), \[ rac{c}{\sqrt n}\le\inf_{\widetilde
u_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde
u_n,
u_P)]\le rac{C}{\sqrt n}.\]

Uniformly for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), the labeled upper and lower bounds on the same gap stratum imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\), \[c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}\le\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]\le C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.\]

Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \[P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0,\qquad M_t(P)=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\qquad \sigma_k(M_t(P))\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2.\] Together with the three observable boundedness conditions in \(\mathcal M\), these implications place its observed margins inside the corresponding uniformly bounded and observably conditioned finite-sample VMW domain. The converse inclusion is not asserted, and this proposition does not resolve gap-free stability on the full VMW class.

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\).  Let \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) be any parameter class in the published VMW model that contains \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\), and, for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), let \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) be any published-VMW parameter class that contains \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\).  Then
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\ge\frac c{\sqrt n}
\]
and, uniformly in \(g\in(0,1/4]\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]
\ge c\min\left\{1,\frac1{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
In particular, both converses transfer to every published-VMW parameter class containing the explicit factorization-preserving witness paths.  This monotonicity transfer does not extend the gap-free modulus, either estimator upper bound, either confidence guarantee, or either matching minimax conclusion beyond \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M(g)\).

Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \[P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0,\qquad M_t(P)=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\qquad \sigma_k(M_t(P))\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2.\] Together with the three observable boundedness conditions in \(\mathcal M\), these implications place its observed margins inside the corresponding uniformly bounded and observably conditioned finite-sample VMW domain. The converse inclusion is not asserted, and this proposition does not resolve gap-free stability on the full VMW class.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), on \(E_P\), the sets \(K_C(P)\), indexed by \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), form a partition of \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\), every \(K_C(P)\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\), and \(I_C\) contains \(\nu_P(K_C(P))\). Moreover, with a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), singleton associated clusters have support-interval length at most \(C r_{n,\alpha}\), their mass intervals have length at most \(C\min\{1,r_{n,\alpha}/\delta(P)\}\), and every associated cluster has \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)\le C\min\{1,r_{n,\alpha}/\Delta_C(P)\}\). Finally, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge1-\alpha\). Thus effects unresolved at the \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\) scale are merged without making the true-cluster association or its external gap implicit.

u_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leho_{n,\alpha}\}\) and the candidate neighborhood \(K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leho_{n,\alpha}\}\). Set \(I_C:=[\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))]\). Define \(\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(
u_P)\setminus K_C(P)\}\), with \(+\infty\) when the complement is empty.

Put \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \(J_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\), and \(q_n:=J_n^{-1}\).  For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse
\[
G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top
\]
and form the total empirical ambient operator
\[
\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all matrices \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) with \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\).  Finally, set
\[
\mathcal P_n:=\left\{J_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{0,\ldots,J_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^ka_u=J_n\right\}
\]
and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-2L,2L]\).  For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\quad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\quad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\quad \lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf1_k\rVert_2.
\]
Order each finite lattice lexicographically, let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first minimizer of \(J_n\), and output \(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\).  This is a total Borel map from every empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), including summaries for which a raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues, to a positive real probability law with at most \(k\) atoms in \([-2L,2L]\).  It is independent of any choice of basis for an empirical signal subspace because it is defined from the ambient thresholded pseudoinverses and a fixed ambient candidate list.  There is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every sample,
\[
W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)
\le C\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost real-arithmetic model, the candidate list has cardinality at most \(C n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\), and exhaustive minimization, including the fixed-size singular-value decompositions and polar decompositions, has polynomial runtime in \(n\).  Consequently, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\), after increasing \(C\) if necessary,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\tag{12}
\]

The library has cardinality at most
\[
C\,n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2},
\]
and exhaustive nearest-library search, including formation of \(\widehat S_n\), uses at most \(C\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\}\) fixed-dimensional arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, and fixed-degree root-isolation operations.  Singular-value thresholding at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) retains exactly the \(k\)-dimensional signal space for every stored representative and remains correct under operator perturbations smaller than \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).  For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the deterministic inequality
\[
W_1(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P)
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\left\{2d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}
\]
holds.  Consequently this explicit finite-library estimator has a collision-uniform root-\(n\) high-probability guarantee, without diagonalizing a possibly nonreal empirical compressed spectrum.

Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\).  Let \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) be any parameter class in the published VMW model that contains \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\), and, for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), let \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) be any published-VMW parameter class that contains \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\).  Then
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\ge\frac c{\sqrt n}
\]
and, uniformly in \(g\in(0,1/4]\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]
\ge c\min\left\{1,\frac1{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
In particular, both converses transfer to every published-VMW parameter class containing the explicit factorization-preserving witness paths.  This monotonicity transfer does not extend the gap-free modulus, either estimator upper bound, either confidence guarantee, or either matching minimax conclusion beyond \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M(g)\).

Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(T=t)&\ge k\pi_0,\\
M_t(P)&=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\\
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V(P)\}&=\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\}\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\\
\sigma_k\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}M_0(P)\\M_1(P)\end{bmatrix}\right)&\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\lVert M_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert N_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert m_X(P)\rVert_2\le L.
\]
With the fixed dimensions and anchor normalization, \(\mathcal M\) is therefore a quantitatively uniform, compact-potential-outcome-support subclass of the published VMW parameter class: VMW Assumption 1 already includes the two proxy conditional independences, causal consistency, and latent ignorability, whereas the present joint latent-arm margin and proxy singular-value margin strengthen the published qualitative positivity and full-rank requirements. The converse inclusion, a gap-free upper bound on the full published VMW class, and a full-class matching minimax conclusion are not asserted.

Put \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \(J_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\), and \(q_n:=J_n^{-1}\).  For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse
\[
G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top
\]
and form the total empirical ambient operator
\[
\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all matrices \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) with \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\).  Finally, set
\[
\mathcal P_n:=\left\{J_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{0,\ldots,J_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^ka_u=J_n\right\}
\]
and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-2L,2L]\).  For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\quad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\quad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\quad \lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf1_k\rVert_2.
\]
Order each finite lattice lexicographically, let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first minimizer of \(J_n\), and output \(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\).  This is a total Borel map from every empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), including summaries for which a raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues, to a positive real probability law with at most \(k\) atoms in \([-2L,2L]\).  It is independent of any choice of basis for an empirical signal subspace because it is defined from the ambient thresholded pseudoinverses and a fixed ambient candidate list.  There is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every sample,
\[
W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)
\le C\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost real-arithmetic model, the candidate list has cardinality at most \(C n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\), and exhaustive minimization, including the fixed-size singular-value decompositions and polar decompositions, has polynomial runtime in \(n\).  Consequently, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\), after increasing \(C\) if necessary,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\tag{12}
\]

In the fixed-dimensional exact-real computational model in which the class-dependent finite library of representative summaries is precomputed, \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) is a total Borel map with values in the positive real probability laws having at most \(k\) atoms.  The library has cardinality at most
\[
C\,n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2},
\]
and exhaustive nearest-library search, including formation of \(\widehat S_n\), uses at most \(C\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\}\) fixed-dimensional arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, and fixed-degree root-isolation operations.  Singular-value thresholding at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) retains exactly the \(k\)-dimensional signal space for every stored representative and remains correct under operator perturbations smaller than \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).  For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the deterministic inequality
\[
W_1(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P)
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\left\{2d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}
\]
holds.  Consequently this explicit finite-library estimator has a collision-uniform root-\(n\) high-probability guarantee, without diagonalizing a possibly nonreal empirical compressed spectrum.

Let \(D:=4d_zd_x+d_x\), \(b:=4\sqrt{d_zd_x}+\sqrt{d_x}\), and \(\epsilon_n:=n^{-1/2}\).  Partition the coordinate box \([-L,L]^D\) into a deterministic lexicographically ordered grid of half-open cubes of side at most \(\epsilon_n/b\).  If \(\mathscr S\ne\varnothing\), from every cube meeting \(\mathscr S\) fix one representative \(q_{n,\ell}\in\mathscr S\), and let \(\widehat q_n\) be the smallest-index minimizer of \(d_S(q_{n,\ell},\widehat S_n)\).  At \(\widehat q_n\), retain the \(k\) right singular directions of the vertically stacked proxy moment whose singular values exceed \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), call the resulting basis \(V\), and form the compressed effect operator \(\Delta\), left anchor \(a\), and right anchor \(c\) by the formulas in \(\mathrm{def:compressed\text{-}operator}\).  For each distinct eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta\), put \(E_\lambda:=\prod_{\gamma\ne\lambda}(\Delta-\gamma I_k)/(\lambda-\gamma)\), with the empty product equal to \(I_k\), and define
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}:=\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta)}a^\top E_\lambda c\,\delta_\lambda.
\]
If \(\mathscr S=\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) to be the unit point mass at zero.

Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\).  Let \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) be any parameter class in the published VMW model that contains \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\), and, for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), let \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) be any published-VMW parameter class that contains \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\).  Then
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\ge\frac c{\sqrt n}
\]
and, uniformly in \(g\in(0,1/4]\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]
\ge c\min\left\{1,\frac1{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
In particular, both converses transfer to every published-VMW parameter class containing the explicit factorization-preserving witness paths.  This monotonicity transfer does not extend the gap-free modulus, either estimator upper bound, either confidence guarantee, or either matching minimax conclusion beyond \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M(g)\).

Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(T=t)&\ge k\pi_0,\\
M_t(P)&=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\\
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V(P)\}&=\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\}\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\\
\sigma_k\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}M_0(P)\\M_1(P)\end{bmatrix}\right)&\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\lVert M_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert N_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert m_X(P)\rVert_2\le L.
\]
With the fixed dimensions and anchor normalization, \(\mathcal M\) is therefore a quantitatively uniform, compact-potential-outcome-support subclass of the published VMW parameter class: VMW Assumption 1 already includes the two proxy conditional independences, causal consistency, and latent ignorability, whereas the present joint latent-arm margin and proxy singular-value margin strengthen the published qualitative positivity and full-rank requirements. The converse inclusion, a gap-free upper bound on the full published VMW class, and a full-class matching minimax conclusion are not asserted.

Put \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \(J_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\), and \(q_n:=J_n^{-1}\).  For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse
\[
G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top
\]
and form the total empirical ambient operator
\[
\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all matrices \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) with \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\).  Finally, set
\[
\mathcal P_n:=\left\{J_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{0,\ldots,J_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^ka_u=J_n\right\}
\]
and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-2L,2L]\).  For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\quad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\quad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\quad \lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf1_k\rVert_2.
\]
Order each finite lattice lexicographically, let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first minimizer of \(J_n\), and output \(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\).  This is a total Borel map from every empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), including summaries for which a raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues, to a positive real probability law with at most \(k\) atoms in \([-2L,2L]\).  It is independent of any choice of basis for an empirical signal subspace because it is defined from the ambient thresholded pseudoinverses and a fixed ambient candidate list.  There is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every sample,
\[
W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)
\le C\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost real-arithmetic model, the candidate list has cardinality at most \(C n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\), and exhaustive minimization, including the fixed-size singular-value decompositions and polar decompositions, has polynomial runtime in \(n\).  Consequently, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\), after increasing \(C\) if necessary,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\tag{12}
\]

In the fixed-dimensional exact-real computational model in which the class-dependent finite library of representative summaries is precomputed, \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) is a total Borel map with values in the positive real probability laws having at most \(k\) atoms.  The library has cardinality at most
\[
C\,n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2},
\]
and exhaustive nearest-library search, including formation of \(\widehat S_n\), uses at most \(C\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\}\) fixed-dimensional arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, and fixed-degree root-isolation operations.  Singular-value thresholding at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) retains exactly the \(k\)-dimensional signal space for every stored representative and remains correct under operator perturbations smaller than \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).  For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), the deterministic inequality
\[
W_1(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P)
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\left\{2d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}
\]
holds.  Consequently this explicit finite-library estimator has a collision-uniform root-\(n\) high-probability guarantee, without diagonalizing a possibly nonreal empirical compressed spectrum.

\[

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\).  Let \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) be any parameter class in the published VMW model that contains \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\), and, for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), let \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) be any published-VMW parameter class that contains \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\).  Then
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\ge\frac c{\sqrt n}
\]
and, uniformly in \(g\in(0,1/4]\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]
\ge c\min\left\{1,\frac1{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
In particular, both converses transfer to every published-VMW parameter class containing the explicit factorization-preserving witness paths.  This monotonicity transfer does not extend the gap-free modulus, either estimator upper bound, either confidence guarantee, or either matching minimax conclusion beyond \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M(g)\).

Every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(T=t)&\ge k\pi_0,\\
M_t(P)&=A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top,\\
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V(P)\}&=\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\}\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\\
\sigma_k\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}M_0(P)\\M_1(P)\end{bmatrix}\right)&\ge\pi_0\sigma_0^2,
\end{aligned}
\qquad
\lVert M_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert N_t(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},\ \lVert m_X(P)\rVert_2\le L.
\]
With the fixed dimensions and anchor normalization, \(\mathcal M\) is a quantitatively uniform conditional-moment subclass of the published VMW parameter class. It retains VMW Assumption 1 in its exact armwise form, including \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\) separately for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), strengthens the published qualitative latent positivity and full-rank requirements to the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\), and adds
\[
\max_{t\in\{0,1\}}\max_{1\le u\le k}\mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|\mid U=u]\le L.
\]
The last condition implies \(|\mu_{tu}|\le L\) and \(|\tau_u|\le2L\), but it imposes neither joint-vector ignorability nor almost-sure potential-outcome support. The converse inclusion and all upper, confidence, cluster, and full-class matching conclusions on the full published VMW class are not asserted; only lower bounds carried by explicit witness paths transfer upward to containing classes.

Put \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \(J_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil\), and \(q_n:=J_n^{-1}\).  For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse
\[
G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top
\]
and form the total empirical ambient operator
\[
\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}
-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all matrices \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) with \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\).  Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\).  Finally, set
\[
\mathcal P_n:=\left\{J_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{0,\ldots,J_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^ka_u=J_n\right\}
\]
and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\).  For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define
\[
D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,
\quad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,
\quad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,
\quad \lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u},
\]
and
\[
J_n(\vartheta):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D_n\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert m_\vartheta-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2
+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf1_k\rVert_2.
\]
Order each finite lattice lexicographically, let \(\widehat\vartheta_n\) be the first minimizer of \(J_n\), and output \(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n}\).  This is a total Borel map from every empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), including summaries for which a raw compressed operator has nonreal eigenvalues, to a positive real probability law with at most \(k\) atoms in \([-L_{\tau},L_{\tau}]\).  It is independent of any choice of basis for an empirical signal subspace because it is defined from the ambient thresholded pseudoinverses and a fixed ambient candidate list.  There is a finite \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) such that, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) and every sample,
\[
W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)
\le C\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost real-arithmetic model, the candidate list has cardinality at most \(C n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\), and exhaustive minimization, including the fixed-size singular-value decompositions and polar decompositions, has polynomial runtime in \(n\).  Consequently, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\), after increasing \(C\) if necessary,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{W_1(\lambda_{\widehat\vartheta_n},\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le\eta.
\tag{12}
\]

snapshot.stmt:
For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), the upper and lower bounds on the same uniformly conditioned causal VMW class imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}\le\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\le\frac{C}{\sqrt n}.
\]

For the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), uniformly for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), the labeled upper and lower bounds on the same gap stratum imply that, for finite \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}\le\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]\le C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]

Can one compute, in time polynomial in \(n\) in the fixed-dimensional real-arithmetic model, the exact confidence set \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), every exact cluster-mass interval \(I_C\), and the full report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) on every empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), including summaries whose raw compressed operator has conjugate nonreal eigenpairs, without compact nearest-summary optimization or evaluation of the abstract extension \(\overline F\)? The polynomial-time positive real law-estimation part is settled by \(\mathrm{prop:polynomial\text{-}net\text{-}law\text{-}estimator}\); this question concerns exact confidence-set and cluster-extremum computation only.

defs.def:cluster-report:
Set \(E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\) and \(ho_{n,\alpha}:=2C_{\mathrm{mod}}r_{n,\alpha}/(2\pi_0)\). Join two atoms of \(\widehat
u_n\) when their distance is at most \(4ho_{n,\alpha}\), and let \(\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) be the connected components. For \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define the true association \(K_C(P):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(
u_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leho_{n,\alpha}\}\) and the candidate neighborhood \(K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\leho_{n,\alpha}\}\). Set \(I_C:=[\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))]\). The report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) contains, for every \(C\), the interval \([\min C-ho_{n,\alpha},\max C+ho_{n,\alpha}]\) and \(I_C\). Define \(\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(
u_P)\setminus K_C(P)\}\), with \(+\infty\) when the complement is empty.

defs.def:constructive-repair-handle: For positive-law repair, start from Bauer--Fike localization of the empirical compressed operator, replace individual eigenvectors inside overlapping discs by Kato contour projectors, transport aggregate projector mass only across each cluster diameter, and project the finite summary onto the positive \(k\)-atomic moment cone before extracting a real probability measure. For the labeled-weight converse, differentiate the Bernoulli factorization of \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and solve the linear score-cancellation equations for proxy and treatment primitives so that a weight displacement \(h\) preserves the factorization while the observed score has order \(g h\).

snapshot.stmt:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\).  Let \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) be any parameter class in the published VMW model that contains \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\), and, for \(g\in(0,1/4]\), let \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}\) be any published-VMW parameter class that contains \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\).  Then
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)]\ge\frac c{\sqrt n}
\]
and, uniformly in \(g\in(0,1/4]\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^{p}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}[\lVert\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\rVert_1]
\ge c\min\left\{1,\frac1{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
In particular, both converses transfer to every published-VMW parameter class containing the explicit factorization-preserving witness paths.  This monotonicity transfer does not extend the gap-free modulus, either estimator upper bound, either confidence guarantee, or either matching minimax conclusion beyond \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M(g)\).
